/w holds a small lookup service built out of a hand-rolled middleware stack. It starts, its
unit tests do not pass, and it does not behave as specified below. Repair it IN PLACE.

What is already there:

  app/router.py      request-target splitting and the route table
  app/store.py       the lookup table, loaded from data/animals.json
  app/negotiate.py   content negotiation and body rendering
  app/middleware.py  the layer plumbing
  app/handlers.py    the route handlers
  app/legacy_handler.py   dead code (see below)
  server.py          the entry point, `python3 server.py <port>`
  tests/test_unit.py the unit tests
  data/animals.json  the data

Rules for the repair:
  - tests/test_unit.py and data/animals.json must NOT be modified, and tests/ must keep exactly
    the two files it has now. All 17 tests must pass: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
    -q` must report "Ran 24 tests" and end with OK.
  - app/legacy_handler.py must be DELETED. Its job (rejecting methods) becomes a middleware
    layer `with_method_guard` in app/middleware.py.
  - When you are done app/ contains exactly six .py files: __init__.py, router.py, store.py,
    negotiate.py, middleware.py, handlers.py. Do not add modules and do not delete any other one.
  - Also create client.py and run.sh in /w (described at the end).

=== The contract every piece must satisfy ===

app/store.py — class Store(path)
  get(name)   the colour for that EXACT name, or None. Lookup is case-sensitive: the data has
              both "panda" and "Panda" and they are different entries.
  names()     the raw keys, sorted ascending by code point.

app/router.py — class Router
  add(method, path, handler)
  split(target) -> (path, params). The path is everything before the first "?", percent-decoded,
              with "+" left alone because a "+" in a path is a literal plus. params maps each
              query key to the FIRST value given for it; keys and values are decoded the query
              way, where "+" IS a space and "%2B" is a literal plus.
  resolve(method, path) -> ("ok", handler) or ("not_found", None)

app/negotiate.py
  choose(accept)  "json" when the Accept header is absent, "*/*" or "application/json";
              "text" when it is exactly "text/plain"; otherwise None.
  render(payload, kind) -> (content_type, body) where body is UTF-8 BYTES.
              kind "json": json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True) encoded
                   UTF-8, content type "application/json".
              kind "text": if payload has both "name" and "color", "<name>: <color>\n";
                   otherwise json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True) + "\n";
                   encoded UTF-8, content type "text/plain; charset=utf-8".

app/middleware.py
  A handler is f(ctx) -> (status, headers, payload). A layer is f(next_handler) -> handler.
  chain(*layers)(inner) composes them so that layers[0] is the OUTERMOST, i.e. it is entered
              first and its next is layers[1].
  AppError(status, payload) is raised by handlers to abort with that reply.
  with_error_envelope   turns an AppError into its (status, {}, payload); any other exception
              into (500, {}, {"error":"internal"}).
  with_content_length   renders the payload with negotiate.render using ctx["kind"], or "json"
              when ctx["kind"] is None, and sets Content-Type plus a Content-Length that is the
              number of BYTES of the rendered body. It leaves a None payload alone.
  with_method_guard     (you add this) replies 405 {"error":"method_not_allowed"} with header
              Allow: "GET, HEAD" for any ctx["method"] other than GET or HEAD, without calling
              the next handler. It must work for EVERY method a client can send, including ones
              the stdlib handler has no do_<METHOD> for, such as DELETE and PATCH.
  LruCache(capacity)    (you add this) a least-recently-used cache.
              get(key)  the stored value, or None. A hit counts as a use.
              put(key, value)  stores it; storing counts as a use, including when the key was
                        already there. When the cache is over capacity it drops entries least
                        recently used first until it fits.
              keys()    the keys held, least recently used FIRST, most recently used last.
  with_cache(cache)     (you add this) a layer FACTORY: with_cache(cache) returns a layer.
              The key is the tuple (ctx["path"], ctx["params"].get("name", ""), ctx["kind"]).
              On a hit it returns the stored (status, headers, payload) without calling the next
              handler, with the header X-Cache: "hit" added. On a miss it calls the next handler
              and, only if that returned status 200, stores the triple and adds X-Cache: "miss".
              A non-200 return is passed through untouched and is not stored, and an exception
              from the next handler is allowed to propagate and stores nothing.

app/handlers.py
  lookup(ctx)   no "name" parameter at all, or an empty one -> AppError(400,
              {"error":"missing_name"}). A name that is not in the store -> AppError(404,
              {"error":"not_found","name":<the name>}). Otherwise (200, {}, {"name":...,
              "color":...}).
  names(ctx)    (you add this) (200, {}, {"names": <store.names()>}).

server.py
  ctx carries "method", "path", "params", "accept", "kind" (from negotiate.choose) and "store".
  The pipeline is chain(with_content_length, with_error_envelope, with_method_guard,
  with_cache(LruCache(3))) around the dispatcher, so that EVERY reply — including 404, 405 and
  500 — leaves with a correct Content-Length, a rejected method never reaches the cache, and a
  failed lookup is never cached.
  Routes: GET /lookup -> lookup, GET /names -> names. An unknown path is AppError(404,
  {"error":"no_route"}); route resolution happens BEFORE negotiation, so an unknown path with an
  unusable Accept is still 404. An unusable Accept on a known path is AppError(406,
  {"error":"not_acceptable"}).
  HEAD is answered exactly like GET, with the same status and the same headers including
  Content-Length, but with no body. The server prints nothing to stdout or stderr.

=== client.py and run.sh ===

`python3 client.py <port>` prints exactly these 15 lines and nothing else:

panda=black-and-white
creme=pâle
plus=rust
literal=grey
case=404
missing=400
noname=400
route=404
method=405:GET, HEAD
text=crème: pâle
notacceptable=406
head=200:45
names=5
cache1=miss
cache2=hit

  panda          GET /lookup?name=panda                    -> the "color" field
  creme          GET /lookup?name=cr%C3%A8me               -> the "color" field
  plus           GET /lookup?name=red+panda                -> the "color" field
  literal        GET /lookup?name=co%2Bala                 -> the "color" field
  case           GET /lookup?name=PANDA                    -> the status code
  missing        GET /lookup                               -> the status code
  noname         GET /lookup?name=                         -> the status code
  route          GET /other                                -> the status code
  method         POST /lookup?name=panda                   -> "<status>:<the Allow header>"
  text           GET /lookup?name=cr%C3%A8me with Accept: text/plain -> the body decoded as
                 UTF-8 with the trailing newline stripped
  notacceptable  GET /lookup?name=panda with Accept: application/xml -> the status code
  head           HEAD /lookup?name=panda                   -> "<status>:<Content-Length header>"
  names          GET /names                                -> how many names came back
  cache1         GET /lookup?name=co%2Bala                  -> the X-Cache header
  cache2         GET /lookup?name=co%2Bala again            -> the X-Cache header

`bash run.sh` starts server.py on port 8716 with all of its output redirected to /dev/null,
waits for the port to accept connections, runs `python3 client.py 8716`, kills the server, and
exits with the client's exit status. The only thing on its stdout is the client's 15 lines.

Run the unit tests and `bash run.sh` yourself before you finish.

"""Unit tests for the lookup service. DO NOT MODIFY THIS FILE.

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -q

Every assertion here is part of the required behaviour. Some of them fail right now.
"""
import importlib
import unittest

from app import negotiate
from app.handlers import lookup, names
from app.middleware import AppError, LruCache, chain, with_cache, with_method_guard
from app.router import Router
from app.store import Store


def ctx(params=None, method="GET", kind="json"):
    return {"method": method, "path": "/lookup", "params": params or {},
            "accept": None, "kind": kind, "store": Store("data/animals.json")}


class TestStore(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_lookup_is_case_sensitive(self):
        s = Store("data/animals.json")
        self.assertEqual(s.get("panda"), "black-and-white")
        self.assertEqual(s.get("Panda"), "impostor")
        self.assertIsNone(s.get("PANDA"))

    def test_names_are_the_raw_keys_sorted_by_codepoint(self):
        s = Store("data/animals.json")
        self.assertEqual(s.names(), ["Panda", "co+ala", "cr\u00e8me", "panda", "red panda"])


class TestRouter(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_query_plus_is_a_space(self):
        r = Router()
        self.assertEqual(r.split("/lookup?name=red+panda")[1]["name"], "red panda")

    def test_percent_2b_stays_a_plus(self):
        r = Router()
        self.assertEqual(r.split("/lookup?name=co%2Bala")[1]["name"], "co+ala")

    def test_path_keeps_its_plus(self):
        r = Router()
        self.assertEqual(r.split("/look+up?x=1")[0], "/look+up")

    def test_first_value_of_a_repeated_key_wins(self):
        r = Router()
        self.assertEqual(r.split("/lookup?name=a&name=b")[1]["name"], "a")


class TestNegotiate(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_render_json_returns_utf8_bytes(self):
        ctype, body = negotiate.render({"name": "cr\u00e8me"}, "json")
        self.assertEqual(ctype, "application/json")
        self.assertIsInstance(body, bytes)
        self.assertEqual(body, '{"name": "cr\u00e8me"}'.encode("utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(len(body), 18)

    def test_render_text_returns_utf8_bytes(self):
        ctype, body = negotiate.render({"name": "cr\u00e8me", "color": "p\u00e2le"}, "text")
        self.assertEqual(ctype, "text/plain; charset=utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(body, "cr\u00e8me: p\u00e2le\n".encode("utf-8"))


class TestChain(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_first_layer_is_the_outermost(self):
        order = []

        def layer(tag):
            def outer(nxt):
                def handler(c):
                    order.append(tag)
                    return nxt(c)
                return handler
            return outer

        built = chain(layer("a"), layer("b"))(lambda c: (200, {}, None))
        built({})
        self.assertEqual(order, ["a", "b"])


class TestMethodGuard(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_post_is_rejected_with_an_allow_header(self):
        guarded = with_method_guard(lambda c: (200, {}, {"ok": True}))
        status, headers, payload = guarded(ctx(method="POST"))
        self.assertEqual(status, 405)
        self.assertEqual(headers.get("Allow"), "GET, HEAD")
        self.assertEqual(payload, {"error": "method_not_allowed"})

    def test_get_and_head_pass_through(self):
        guarded = with_method_guard(lambda c: (200, {}, {"ok": True}))
        self.assertEqual(guarded(ctx(method="GET"))[0], 200)
        self.assertEqual(guarded(ctx(method="HEAD"))[0], 200)


class TestLru(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_keys_are_least_recently_used_first(self):
        c = LruCache(3)
        c.put("a", 1)
        c.put("b", 2)
        c.put("c", 3)
        self.assertEqual(c.keys(), ["a", "b", "c"])

    def test_reading_a_key_refreshes_it(self):
        c = LruCache(3)
        c.put("a", 1)
        c.put("b", 2)
        c.put("c", 3)
        self.assertEqual(c.get("a"), 1)
        self.assertEqual(c.keys(), ["b", "c", "a"])

    def test_writing_an_existing_key_refreshes_it(self):
        c = LruCache(2)
        c.put("a", 1)
        c.put("b", 2)
        c.put("a", 9)
        self.assertEqual(c.keys(), ["b", "a"])
        self.assertEqual(c.get("a"), 9)

    def test_eviction_drops_the_least_recently_used(self):
        c = LruCache(2)
        c.put("a", 1)
        c.put("b", 2)
        c.get("a")
        c.put("c", 3)
        self.assertEqual(c.keys(), ["a", "c"])
        self.assertIsNone(c.get("b"))


class TestCacheLayer(unittest.TestCase):
    def inner(self, calls):
        def handler(c):
            calls.append(c["params"].get("name"))
            return 200, {}, {"name": c["params"].get("name")}
        return handler

    def test_second_identical_request_is_a_hit(self):
        calls = []
        h = with_cache(LruCache(3))(self.inner(calls))
        first = h(ctx({"name": "panda"}))
        second = h(ctx({"name": "panda"}))
        self.assertEqual(first[1].get("X-Cache"), "miss")
        self.assertEqual(second[1].get("X-Cache"), "hit")
        self.assertEqual(calls, ["panda"])

    def test_a_different_kind_is_a_different_entry(self):
        calls = []
        h = with_cache(LruCache(3))(self.inner(calls))
        h(ctx({"name": "panda"}, kind="json"))
        out = h(ctx({"name": "panda"}, kind="text"))
        self.assertEqual(out[1].get("X-Cache"), "miss")
        self.assertEqual(calls, ["panda", "panda"])

    def test_a_raising_handler_caches_nothing(self):
        def boom(c):
            raise AppError(404, {"error": "not_found"})
        cache = LruCache(3)
        h = with_cache(cache)(boom)
        with self.assertRaises(AppError):
            h(ctx({"name": "zzz"}))
        self.assertEqual(cache.keys(), [])


class TestHandlers(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_missing_name_is_400_not_404(self):
        with self.assertRaises(AppError) as cm:
            lookup(ctx({}))
        self.assertEqual(cm.exception.status, 400)
        self.assertEqual(cm.exception.payload, {"error": "missing_name"})

    def test_empty_name_is_400(self):
        with self.assertRaises(AppError) as cm:
            lookup(ctx({"name": ""}))
        self.assertEqual(cm.exception.status, 400)

    def test_unknown_name_is_404_and_echoes_it(self):
        with self.assertRaises(AppError) as cm:
            lookup(ctx({"name": "zzz"}))
        self.assertEqual(cm.exception.status, 404)
        self.assertEqual(cm.exception.payload, {"error": "not_found", "name": "zzz"})

    def test_hit(self):
        self.assertEqual(lookup(ctx({"name": "red panda"})),
                         (200, {}, {"name": "red panda", "color": "rust"}))

    def test_names_handler(self):
        status, headers, payload = names(ctx({}))
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(payload, {"names": ["Panda", "co+ala", "cr\u00e8me", "panda", "red panda"]})


class TestLegacyIsGone(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_legacy_handler_module_no_longer_exists(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ImportError):
            importlib.import_module("app.legacy_handler")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def wait(port, t=20):
    end = time.time() + t
    while time.time() < end:

        rc = s.connect_ex(("127.0.0.1", port)); s.close()

def req(port, path, method="GET", headers=None, timeout=8):

    for k, v in (headers or {}).items(): r.add_header(k, v)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(r, timeout=timeout) as resp:
